slot.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slot.brief: Find B at the centre of a regular polygon of wire carrying current, using superposition of the finite-segment formula.

stem: A square wire loop of side $20$ cm carries a current $I$. If the magnetic field at its centre is $40\sqrt{2}\ \mu$T, the value of $I$ is:

verdicts.working: For each side, the centre is a distance 0.1 m away and the endpoint angles are 45°. Thus the total field is B = 4[μ₀I/(4π·0.1)](2 sin 45°) = 4√2 I μT. Equating to 40√2 μT gives I = 10 A.

working:
$a=0.10$ m; each side subtends $45^\circ$ at either end.
$B=4\left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}(2\sin45^\circ)\right)=\dfrac{\mu_0 I\sqrt{2}}{\pi a}=4\sqrt{2}I\ \mu$T.
$4\sqrt{2}I=40\sqrt{2}\;\Rightarrow\; I=10$ A.

Independent check: For each side, the centre is a distance 0.1 m away and the endpoint angles are 45°. Thus the total field is B = 4[μ₀I/(4π·0.1)](2 sin 45°) = 4√2 I μT. Equating to 40√2 μT gives I = 10 A.
solution:
For one side, $B_1=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}(2\sin45^\circ)$, where $a=0.10\,\text{m}$. Thus, for four sides,
$$B=4B_1=4\sqrt{2}I\,\mu\text{T}.$$
Equating to $40\sqrt{2}\,\mu\text{T}$ gives $I=10\,\text{A}$.
